ref_extractions.title: Age and sex modulate the variability of neural responses to naturalistic videos
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This 2017 bioRxiv paper by Petroni et al. includes authors Milham and Parra who are central to the HBN-EEG project, and studies neural responses to naturalistic videos using EEG. However, the sample size (N=114) and publication year (2017) precede the openneuro_ds005512 release (Release 8, 2025). It is unclear whether this study used an early version of HBN-EEG that maps to this specific dataset release, or a separate earlier collection.
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Authors are HBN-EEG collaborators; paper predates current dataset release. Dataset match uncertain.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Inter-subject correlation analysis of EEG responses to classroom and Hollywood videos in N=114 subjects (5-44 years); primary outcome is neural variability as a function of age/sex.

ref_extractions.title: HBN-EEG: The FAIR implementation of the Healthy Brain Network (HBN) electroencephalography dataset
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This 2024 bioRxiv paper by Shirazi et al. is the official documentation paper for the HBN-EEG data release pipeline. It explicitly lists https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds005512 as one of the nine current dataset releases, and describes the complete dataset structure, six tasks (including contrast detection, resting state, movie watching), HED annotations, and available psychopathology dimensions. It defines the dataset architecture but does not itself run an ML prediction task.
ref_extractions.paradigm: multi-task battery (resting, movie watching, contrast detection, surround suppression, sequence learning, symbol search)
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Primary documentation paper for the HBN-EEG dataset ecosystem including ds005512.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Describes FAIR implementation of HBN-EEG BIDS-formatted data with HED annotations, 6 tasks, demographic variables, and 4 psychopathology dimensions (internalizing, externalizing, attention, p-factor). Lists all 9 OpenNeuro dataset URLs including ds005512.

ref_extractions.title: An open resource for transdiagnostic research in pediatric mental health and learning disorders

It mentions EEG as part of the multimodal battery but does not focus on EEG data, does not reference the specific openneuro_ds005512 dataset, and does not define any EEG-based ML task. ref_extractions.evidence_desc: HBN Biobank overview paper describing recruitment, protocol, and initial data release structure across multiple modalities including MRI, EEG, eye tracking, and genetics.

ref_extractions.title: A resource for assessing information processing in the developing brain using EEG and eye tracking
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This Scientific Data paper (Langer et al., 2017) describes a high-density EEG and eye-tracking battery dataset of 126 subjects (ages 6-44) with passive and active tasks. This appears to be the initial pilot/prototype for the later HBN-EEG multi-task battery. The paradigm description closely matches tasks later included in HBN-EEG (resting state, surround suppression, videos, contrast detection, sequence learning). However, the sample (N=126) is much smaller than openneuro_ds005512 (N=257+ subjects), and the paper explicitly describes this as a single initial release distinct from the full HBN Biobank. The relationship to the specific ds005512 release is suggestive but not definitive.
ref_extractions.paradigm: multi-task battery (resting state, surround suppression, videos, contrast detection, sequence learning, symbol search)
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Appears to be a precursor/pilot dataset (N=126) for the later full HBN-EEG battery that grew into the openneuro_ds005512 release. Paradigms match but sample size differs.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: EEG and eye tracking dataset with 126 subjects, 6 paradigms spanning passive/active and simple/complex dimensions, including cognitive test battery and psychiatric questionnaires.

ref_extractions.title: Functional connectivity of EEG is subject-specific, associated with phenotype, and different from fMRI
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This NeuroImage paper by Nentwich et al. analyzes EEG functional connectivity using phase-coupling from the Healthy Brain Network Biobank. It reports on 1,657 participants (5-21 years) from HBN and examines FC-phenotype associations (age, sex, IQ, ADHD, socioeconomic status, anxiety). It uses resting state, video viewing, and visual flicker tasks. The sample size (1,657) exceeds openneuro_ds005512 (257 subjects), suggesting it uses an earlier/larger HBN EEG data release, not specifically the ds005512 dataset. It defines EEG FC as the primary measure but does not frame a concrete ML classification/regression task for psychiatric diagnosis prediction.
ref_extractions.paradigm: resting state, video viewing, visual flicker (EEG functional connectivity analysis)
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Uses HBN EEG data but from an earlier release (N=1,657), not specifically ds005512. FC analysis rather than classification task.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Phase-coupling (iCOH) functional connectivity analysis of EEG across tasks; associations with demographic and phenotypic variables; comparison with fMRI connectivity.

ref_extractions.title: A benchmark for prediction of psychiatric multimorbidity from resting EEG data in a large pediatric sample
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This NeuroImage paper by Langer et al. (2022) presents a machine learning benchmark challenge using HBN EEG data. It explicitly references the Healthy Brain Network (HBN) initiative and defines two concrete ML tasks: (1) multi-task multi-label classification of 7 DSM-V psychiatric diagnoses using resting EEG and demographics, and (2) multiple regression for psychiatric symptom severity using behavioral/cognitive measures. The paper describes the data as coming from HBN (N=2,042), which is consistent with the larger HBN-EEG ecosystem that includes openneuro_ds005512 (Release 8 with 257+ subjects). The paradigm is resting-state EEG epoched from instructed eyes-closed periods.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: tmin=0s, tmax=40s, overlap=0.95 (generating 2s epochs with ~0.1s step)
ref_extractions.label_mapping: DSM-V diagnosis columns → binary labels for 7 diagnostic categories; symptom severity dimensions → continuous regression targets
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Defines concrete ML benchmark tasks using HBN resting EEG. Sample size (N~2,042) from earlier releases; openneuro_ds005512 is a later release from the same dataset ecosystem.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Multi-label classification of 7 DSM-V diagnoses (ADHD, ODD, anxiety disorder, mood disorder, autism spectrum disorder, specific learning disorder, communication disorder) and regression on symptom severity from resting EEG epochs and demographic features.

feasibility_reason: The dataset has clear event structure with resting-state events (instructed_toCloseEyes, resting_start) and clinical DSM-V diagnostic labels available via the misc route. Reference paper_10_1016_j_neuroimage_2022_119348.pdf provides direct evidence of multi-label psychiatric diagnosis classification from resting EEG being performed on this paradigm, supporting the Classical Task 1 described in analysis.md.
tasks_section:
## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Psychiatric Diagnosis Classification from Resting EEG
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_long_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0 s, tmax = 40 s, overlap = 0.95 (generating 2s epochs with ~0.1s step), target_events = [`instructed_toCloseEyes`, `resting_start`]
- **Label Route**: `misc`
- **Meta Level**: super
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | DSM-V diagnosis column | 0 | No diagnosis (neurotypical) |
  | DSM-V diagnosis column | 1 | Presence of diagnosis (ADHD/ODD/ANX/MDD/ASD/SLD/CD) |
- **Super Meta Notes**: Derived from clinical DSM-V diagnostic assessments stored as multi-label binary vectors (7 diagnostic categories). Kernel step: Concatenate eyes-closed resting blocks per subject, extract 2s epochs with ~0.1s step (~95% overlap), compute spectral power features in canonical bands (delta 1–4 Hz, theta 4–8 Hz, alpha 8–13 Hz, beta 13–30 Hz, gamma 30–40 Hz), predict 7 binary diagnosis labels via multi-output classifier. Ensure subject-wise train/test splits to prevent label leakage across diagnostic categories.
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2022.119348 — Multi-label classification benchmark of 7 DSM-V psychiatric diagnoses from resting EEG (eyes-closed blocks, 2s epochs, 1–40 Hz spectral features, N~2,042 subjects)
- **Kernel Notes**: Filter for `instructed_toCloseEyes` or `resting_start` events (eyes-closed resting segments). Extract 2s epochs with ~0.1s step to achieve ~95% overlap per 40s block. Compute spectral power in canonical frequency bands. Use multi-label classification (binary relevance or multi-output approach). Store DSM-V diagnostic label derivation source and version metadata. Ensure subject-wise data splits to prevent leakage. (replaces Classical Tasks 1–3 from original analysis.md)

### Normal Task 1: Contrast Detection Sensory ERP Analysis
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s, overlap = null, target_events = [`stim_ON`, `left_target`, `right_target`, `fixpoint_ON`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `left_target` | 0 | Left-side target stimulus |
  | `right_target` | 1 | Right-side target stimulus |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 — HBN-EEG dataset documentation listing contrast detection as a primary task paradigm with `stim_ON`, `fixpoint_ON`, `left_target`, `right_target` events annotated in BIDS/HED format
  - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2017.40 — Original HBN dataset description including contrast detection task paradigm for assessing information processing in developing brain
- **Kernel Notes**: Align epochs to `stim_ON` for stimulus-locked analysis (n=22,981) or to `fixpoint_ON` for trial-cue-locked analysis. Note slight count mismatch between `stim_ON` (22,981) and `fixpoint_ON` (22,913) suggests some trials have stimuli without preceding fixation. Filter out admin events (9999, boundary, break cnt) from epoch extraction. Contrast detection includes dot stimuli (dot_no1-8_ON/OFF) suggesting multi-level contrast paradigm; consider separate analysis by contrast level if label metadata available. Button presses (`left_buttonPress`, `right_buttonPress`) can be used for response-locked analysis.

### Normal Task 2: Eyes-Open vs Eyes-Closed Resting State Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_long_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = 2.0 s, overlap = 0.5, target_events = [`instructed_toOpenEyes`, `instructed_toCloseEyes`, `resting_start`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `instructed_toOpenEyes` | 0 | Eyes-open resting state |
  | `instructed_toCloseEyes` | 1 | Eyes-closed resting state |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 — HBN-EEG paradigm documentation describing eyes-open/closed resting state blocks marked by instruction events
  - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2017.40 — Original HBN resource describing resting state EEG with eyes-open/closed conditions
- **Kernel Notes**: Extract 2s epochs with 50% overlap from instruction markers. Use 2s window to capture alpha band differences between eyes-open (suppressed alpha) and eyes-closed (enhanced alpha) states. Note `resting_start` (n=223) is fewer than instruction events (instructed_toCloseEyes: 1,104; instructed_toOpenEyes: 1,326) indicating some resting periods lack explicit block-onset markers; use instruction events as primary triggers. Filter out `9999`, `boundary`, and `break cnt` admin events.

### Potential Task 1: Sequence Learning Block Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_long_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = 10.0 s, overlap = 0.5, target_events = [`seqLearning_start`, `learningBlock_1`, `learningBlock_2`, `learningBlock_3`, `learningBlock_4`, `learningBlock_5`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `learningBlock_1` | 0 | Sequence learning block 1 |
  | `learningBlock_2` | 1 | Sequence learning block 2 |
  | `learningBlock_3` | 2 | Sequence learning block 3 |
  | `learningBlock_4` | 3 | Sequence learning block 4 |
  | `learningBlock_5` | 4 | Sequence learning block 5 |
- **Evidence**: Partial support from DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2017.40 (HBN paradigm description includes sequence learning task) and DOI: https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 (lists sequence learning among HBN-EEG tasks)
- **Kernel Notes**: Extract epochs per learning block (5 blocks per subject, ~200 subjects). Blocks 1–5 may represent different learning phases or conditions; verify against paradigm documentation. Use spectral features or event-related spectral perturbations (ERSP) to track learning-related oscillatory changes (theta, alpha bands). Filter admin events.

### Potential Task 2: Symbol Search Task Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_long_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = 5.0 s, overlap = 0.5, target_events = [`symbolSearch_start`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `symbolSearch_start` | 0 | Symbol search task block onset |
- **Evidence**: Paradigm listed in DOI: https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 and DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2017.40 as one of six HBN tasks; event `symbolSearch_start` present in dataset (n=144)
- **Kernel Notes**: Single event type limits within-task classification; consider cross-task generalization or comparison with resting baseline. Symbol search is an active cognitive task engaging visual search and working memory processes. Relatively few events (n=144) suggests block-level analysis rather than trial-level. Extract spectral features to characterize task-related changes from resting baseline.

### Potential Task 3: Surrounding Suppression Paradigm Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_long_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = 10.0 s, overlap = 0.5, target_events = [`surroundSuppB1_start`, `surroundSuppB2_start`, `contrastChangeB1_start`, `contrastChangeB2_start`, `contrastChangeB3_start`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `surroundSuppB1_start` | 0 | Surrounding suppression block 1 |
  | `surroundSuppB2_start` | 1 | Surrounding suppression block 2 |
  | `contrastChangeB1_start` | 2 | Contrast change block 1 |
  | `contrastChangeB2_start` | 3 | Contrast change block 2 |
  | `contrastChangeB3_start` | 4 | Contrast change block 3 |
- **Evidence**: Paradigm described in DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2017.40 (surround suppression as HBN paradigm for studying visual information processing); events present in dataset
- **Kernel Notes**: Surrounding suppression and contrast change appear related (both involving visual contrast manipulation). Consider combining into single multi-class task or analyzing separately. Blocks B1–B3 and B1–B2 may represent different contrast levels or conditions. Extract event-related spectral changes in gamma band (associated with spatial surround suppression). Filter admin events.
